name: Munenori Kawasaki
facts: Famous for his high-energy post-game interviews and 'I am Japanese!' catchphrase.
Authored a 'handbook' on how to be a teammate.
Once told reporters his secret to avoiding cramps was eating three bananas a day.

name: Ken Harvey
facts: The lone representative for the Royals in the 2004 All-Star Game.
The guy you would not want charging the mound at you before Jorge Soler became that guy.

name: Willie Bloomquist
facts: Played for and coached the Arizona State Sundevils baseball team.
The ultimate utility man. He played multiple positions throughout his career.
Kindof looks like Derek Lowe and Justin Verlander had a baby.

name: Jason Bay
teams: Padres, Pirates, Red Sox, Mets, Mariners
facts: Canadian
The first Pirate to win the National League Rookie of the Year award since Barry Bonds in 1986. The last Pirate to win the award prior to Paul Skenes.
About equally as attractive as Paul Skenes.

name: Esteban Loaiza
teams: Pirates, Rangers, Blue Jays, White Sox, Yankees, Nationals, A's, Dodgers
facts: Married to Mexican Singer Jenni Rivera until her death in 2012. Who? Ask any 40+ year old Mexican woman about Jenni Rivera.
Was arrested for possessing over 40 pounds (yes 40 pounds) of cocaine in 2018 and sentenced to 3 years in prison.
Upon his release from prison, he was deported in 2021 before being deported was cool

name: Mike Cameron
teams: White Sox, Reds, Mariners, Mets, Padres, Brewers, Red Sox, Marlins
facts: One of the key trailblazers in the tilted cap movement that was recently concluded by Fernando Rodney.
Played eight different teams in his 17-year career, but is most remembered for his time with the Seattle Mariners.
Notably took over for Ken Griffey Jr. in center field for the Mariners after Griffey was traded to the Reds.

name: Lyle Overbay
teams: Diamondbacks, Brewers, Blue Jays, Pirates, Yankees, Braves
facts: Although just a rookie bench warmer, he was a member of the 2001 World Series Champion Arizona Diamondbacks.
Finished his career with a 0.00 ERA after retiring Ryan Doumit, the only batter faced in his lone pitching appearance.
Known as Lyle Overpaid for his large contract with the Blue Jays.

name: Miguel Cairo
teams: Blue Jays, Cubs, Cardinals, Yankees, Mets, Mariners, Phillies, Reds
facts: As does any Venezuelan born in the 1970s, he has ten siblings.
The true personification of a 'that guy is still around?' player come every opening day during the 2000s.

name: Ronnie Belliard
teams: Brewers, Rockies, Indians, Cardinals, Nationals, Dodgers
facts: Nicknamed 'La Pared' (The Wall) for his defensive skillset.
Was a member of the 2006 World Series Champion Cardinals.
The Dodgers put a clause in his contract that he had to stay under 210 pounds.

name: Fernando Vina
facts: Made an appearance in the 'Welcome to Atlanta (Coast 2 Coast Remix)' music video by Jermaine Dupri featuring Nelly and the St. Lunatics
Posted an incredibly low 6.2% strikeout percentage over his career.
While his mom was pregnant with him, she attempted to flee Cuba twice on a boat. Eventually his parents were successful and arrived in Key West in 1968.

name: Ryan Klesko
facts: Looked more like the lead singer of 90's post-grunge band than a baseball player.
Was a member of the 1995 World Series Champion Braves.
In 2014 he was inducted into the National Polish-American Sports Hall of Fame in Troy, Michigan, an honor shared with A.J. Pierzynski.

name: Khalil Greene
facts: Looks absolutely nothing like his name is Khalil Greene.
Sean Penn doppelganger. (Look up Spicoli from Fast Times at Ridgemont High.)
Won the 2002 Golden Spikes award at Clemson.

name: Nick Punto
teams: Phillies, Twins, Cardinals, Red Sox, Dodgers, Athletics
facts: The ultimate hustle guy. Commonly known for diving everywhere and sliding headfirst into first base.
Won the 2011 World Series with the St. Louis Cardinals.
Had 3253 at bats over his career but only hit 19 home runs.

name: Trot Nixon
facts: Full name is Christopher Trotman Nixon.
Looks exactly like his name is Trot Nixon, unlike Khalil Greene (see Khalil Greene from July 31).
Member of the 2004 World Series Champion Red Sox.

name: Shea Hillenbrand
teams: Red Sox, Diamondbacks, Blue Jays, Giants, Angels, Dodgers
facts: Owns a 38-acre farm in Gilbert, Arizona, housing over 90 animals including a Galapagos tortoise, an Australian wallaby, miniature horses, and llamas
Appeared on House Hunter's International in 2017 with his second wife, where they were looking for a home in the Dominican Republic.
Openly criticized the Blue Jays' organization for not congratulating him on adopting a daughter. This weird incident basically ruined his relationship with the team and led to his departure in 2006.

name: Richie Sexson
facts: Measured 6 feet 8 inches tall.
Arrested in Clark County, Washington for Driving Under the Influence in 2005.
Nicknamed 'Big Sexy'.

name: Placido Polanco
facts: Set a major league milestone by playing 186 consecutive error-free games at second base, spanning 911 total defensive chances from 2006 to 2007.
Became a U.S. citizen in 2017 while wearing a Detroit Tigers jersey at Comerica Park.
Loved to choke up on the bat; arguably a lost art in today's game.

name: Wes Helms
facts: Managed the Triple A Charlotte Knights after his playing career.
Part of the 2006 Marlins that started nine rookies, earning him the nickname 'Uncle Wes' as the elder veteran among the team.
Honestly a very boring player. Did a solid twelve years in the majors without doing anything notable.

name: Rafael Furcal
facts: Lied about his age as an Amateur Dominican baseball player, claiming to be 19 years old when he was actually 22.

Was arrested for a DUI in a Kroger's parking lot in 2000. He was going to be charged with minor in consumption at the time as well, but his real birth certificate showing his age proved him to be 22 years old.
In 2025, (this time in a Publix grocery store parking lot) he was charged with aggravated battery with a deadly weapon for throwing rocks and a plastic bottle at a truck driver.

name: So Taguchi
facts: Only Cardinals player in history to wear the #99.
Learned English by watching animated movies like Finding Nemo and Monsters Inc..
Won 2 World Series - 2006 with the Cardinals and 2008 with the Phillies.

name: Mike MacDougal
teams: Royals, White Sox, Nationals, Cardinals, Dodgers
facts: His real name is Robert Meiklejohn MacDougal.

In 2002 while playing for the Royals, he was in the dugout while Carlos Beltran was up to bat. Beltran swang the bat and lost his grip which resulted in the bat flying and hitting Macdougal square in the skull. He suffered a cracked skull right above his right temple.
A member of the Wake Forest Sports Hall of Fame.

name: Cesar Izturis
teams: Blue Jays, Dodgers, Cubs, Pirates, Cardinals, Orioles, Brewers, Nationals, Reds
facts: Was traded from the Dodgers to the Cubs in exchange for Greg Maddux.
The first player in MLB history to have a last name that starts with 'I' and ends with 'S' until 2004 when his brother Maicer Izturis debuted with the Montreal Expos.
Serves as a bench coach for the Toros de Tijuana in the Liga Mexicana del Pacífico.

name: Aaron Rowand
facts: Won the 2005 World Series with the Chicago White Sox and again in 2010 with the San Francisco Giants.
Is cousins with former pitcher James Shields.
On May 11, 2006 he made his signature wall-crashing catch, breaking his nose and facial bones while simultaneously denting the 'M' in the 'W.B. Mason' sign in Philadelphia.

name: Hank Blalock
facts: While playing in the minors for the Rangers', he hit for the cycle twice in one week.
Had a fan club called 'Hank's Homies,' a group of Rangers fans who wore cowboy hats, eyeblack, and Blalock jerseys.
Played third base while Alex Rodriguez manned Shortstop for the early part of his time with the Rangers.

name: Delmon Young
facts: Was the first overall pick in the 2003 MLB Draft by the Tampa Bay Devil Rays.
Younger brother of former MLB player Dmitri Young.

Was arrested in 20212 in New York City for aggravated harassment after shouting antisemitic slurs and tackling a man during an drunk dispute. Four years later in Miami, he doubled down on his stupidity and faced battery charges for choking a hotel valet and using anti-Hispanic slurs, though that case was eventually dismissed.

name: Dmitri Young
facts: Older brother of yesterday's Daily Dugout Dude, Delmon Young.
Nicknamed Dmitri 'Da Meat Hook' Young.
Made a memorable appearance at WWE's Survivor Series 2005.
Weighed 295 at his peak weight during his playing career.

Just like his brother's legal troubles Dmitri had his own issues - He was sentenced to one year of probation following a 2006 misdemeanor domestic violence arrest in Michigan. Then again in 2010, he faced misdemeanor charges in Illinois for possession of marijuana and drug paraphernalia.

name: Danny Graves
facts: Born in Saigon, Vietnam, he is the only Vietnamese born player in Major League Baseball history.

Helped build Vietnam's first baseball field in 2006 with the Vietnam Veterans Memorial Fund. As of today, this baseball field has been converted into a soccer field. Great job Vietnam and great job Danny.
Was inducted into the Cincinnati Reds Hall of Fame in 2023.

name: Walter Young
facts: Chose to sign with the Pittsburgh Pirates after the 1999 draft over his football scholarship to play Defensive End for LSU.
Listed as 6'5 322 pounds while playing for the Orioles. He is the heaviest player in Major League Baseball history to date.
Following his ten games with the Orioles, he quit baseball in 2010 and joined the Forrest County Sheriff's Department in Mississippi and began working as a shift sergeant at the county jail.

After what I could only assume was a terribly ineffective career as a shift sergeant based on his weight, he died on September 19, 2015, of a heart attack. He weighed 450 pounds at the time of his death.

name: Jason Kendall
facts: Typically batted leadoff for the Pirates. Uncommon for a catcher.
Holds the record for most stolen bases by a catcher with 189.
Born on June 26, 1974. The exact same date as Derek Jeter.

name: Rocco Baldelli
facts: Member of the Rhode Island Italian-American Hall of Fame. An honor shared with Jay Leno.
Managed the Minnesota Twins from 2019-2025.
Diagnosed with a rare metabolic disorder called mitochondrial disease in 2007, which caused him to miss most of the 2007 and 2008 seasons.

name: Reggie Sanders
teams: Reds, Padres, Braves, Diamondbacks, Giants, Pirates, Cardinals, Royals
facts: Played in the World Series for three teams in a four year span - Diamondbacks 2001, Giants 2002, and Cardinals in 2004.
Was the fifth member of the MLB's illustrious 300/300 club.
Has an autistic brother.

name: Ted Lilly
teams: Expos, Yankees, Athletics, Bluejays, Cubs, Dodgers, Jays
facts: Tried to play in the Venezuelan Winter League in 2013 to prove he still had it...he did not and retired shortly after that stint.
His full name is Theodore Roosevelt Lilly III.
Was charged with three counts of felony insurance fraud in January 2015.

name: Scott Rolen
facts: Every single one of his 17,000+ professional defensive innings came strictly at third base.
The first Daily Dugout Dude that is a member of the MLB Hall of Fame.
Originally had committed to play baseball at Georgia before getting drafted in the second round by the Phillies.

name: Xavier Nady
teams: Padres, Mets, Pirates, Yankees, Cubs, Diamondbacks, Nationals, Giants
facts: His full name is Xavier Clifford Nady VI.
Was a UC Berkley baseball legend. He left as the school's all-time leader in home runs (57), RBIs (191), total bases (479), and slugging percentage (.729).
World Series champion with the SF Giants in 2012.

name: Grady Sizemore
facts: In 2023, after retiring, he accepted a $15/hour internship with the Diamondbacks to stay close to the game.
Was the interim manager for the White Sox in 2024 after the team fired Pedro Grifol.
Ah yes, the picture...in 2009 his playboy playmate girlfriend, Brittany Binger, had her email hacked by a stalker. The hacker found this picture of Grady Sizemore and leaked it.

name: Mark Grudzielanek
teams: Expos, Dodgers, Cubs, Cardinals, Royals, Indians
facts: Won a Gold Glove with the Royals in 2006.
A member of the illustrious National Polish-American Sports Hall of Fame. The honor shared with fellow former DDD, Ryan Klesko.
Was moved to play second base upon arriving to play for the Dodgers so that Alex Cora could play shortstop.

name: LaTroy Hawkins
teams: Twins, Cubs, Giants, Orioles, Rockies, Yankees, Astros, Brewers, Angels, Mets, Blue Jays
facts: In May 2025 he received his bachelor's degree from Southern New Hampshire University. The honor shared with thousands of military wives and single mothers across the country.
He is the Godfather of Patrick Mahomes II, 3 time Super Bowl champion.
He has gotten a Save against every MLB team.

name: Matt Stairs
teams: Expos, Red Sox, Athletics, Cubs, Brewers, Pirates, Royals, Rangers, Tigers, Blue Jays, Phillies, Padres, Nationals
facts: Holds the all time record for pinch hit home runs with 23.
A member of the Canadian Baseball Hall of Fame, an honr shared with former DDD, Jason Bay.
Coached high school hockey in Canada at Fredericton High School in 2012.

name: Carlos Delgado
facts: Doing his best Kaepernick impression, he famously protested the Iraq War by refusing to stand during the playing of 'God Bless America' during the 2004 season.
Holds the MLB record for most home runs by a Puerto Rican.
Finished second in the AL MVP voting to Alex Rodriguez in 2003.

name: Gerald Laird
facts: During 2007 Spring Training, teammate Jerry Hairston Jr. had real police officers fake-arrest a crying Laird over unpaid child support as an elaborate clubhouse prank.
One of the most successful mouth breathers in baseball history (find me a pic of him with his mouth closed...impossible).
Signed with the Tijuana Toros in 2016 after he couldn't find a spot in the majors. He went 0-1 in two appearances and then retired.

name: Yuniesky Betancourt
facts: Wins the award for most flawless skin.

Fled Cuba in 2003 by speed boat. Landed in Cancun, Mexico. Went to jail in Mexico for possessing a fake Mexican passport. Finally released from Mexican jail three weeks later before crossing into the US and claiming political asylum to then start his MLB career.
Most recently, was arrested in 2024 in Miami for staging a fake car crash and is facing felony insurance fraud charges.

name: Jose Vidro
facts: Montreal Expos first DH in interleague play in 1997.
The face of the Montreal to Washington DC transition.
One of three MLB players from Sabana Grande, Puerto Rico. 'Sabana Grande' translates to 'big bedsheet'.

name: Boof Bonser
facts: After his relatively short MLB career, he transitioned into a career as a pipe-fitter helping build submarines for the U.S. government in Connecticut.
Was born John Paul Bonser but legally changed his name to Boof Bonser in 2001.
Part of the franchise-altering trade between the Twins and Giants in which the Giants sent him, Joe Nathan, and Francisco Liriano to the Twins in exchange for A.J. Pierzynski.

name: Sidney Ponson
teams: Orioles, Giants, Cardinals, Yankees, Twins, Rangers, Royals
facts: To all of our surprise, he was born in Aruba and was Knighted in the order of Orange-Nassau by Queen Beatrix of Netherlands.

To none of our surprise based on his appearance, he was arrested three times in the span of nine months in 2004-2005. Once for assaulting a judge in Aruba following a complaint about how he handled his speedboat and two DUIs.
Busted by the International Baseball Federation for using the obesity-fighting drug phentermine.

name: Willie Mo Pena
teams: Reds, Red Sox, Nationals, Diamondbacks, Mariners
facts: Finished his 10-year MLB career with 559 strikeouts and only 425 hits.
Hit bombs. Among his notable home runs provoked by his raw power was a 498-foot blast while playing for the Reds. One of this century's longest home runs.
Not shockingly, the NPB in Japan took a liking to him and his playing style. He was a two time all star during his five year stint in Japan.
